title: What If We Flooded Part of the Sahara? The Plan Needed 213 Nukes

scenes.text: What if we flooded part of the Sahara with the sea? Egypt nearly did, with 213 nuclear bombs.
The Qattara Depression in Egypt sits about sixty meters below sea level. The Mediterranean is only 55 to 100 kilometers away.
scenes.keywords: desert salt flat below sea level

scenes.text: Dig a canal and seawater pours downhill through turbines. First phase: 670 megawatts. The idea dates to 1927.
In 1957 the CIA pitched it to Eisenhower. He said no. In the 1970s a German engineer proposed digging the canal with 213 nuclear bombs.
The lake would take about ten years to fill, then stop rising, because the desert sun evaporates water as fast as it flows in.
Egypt refused the bombs, and the canal alone cost too much. So the Sahara keeps its hole, two hundred feet deep, waiting for the sea.

description:
What if we flooded part of the Sahara with seawater? The Qattara Depression in Egypt lies about 60 meters below sea level, and since 1927 engineers have proposed a 55 to 100 kilometer canal from the Mediterranean to fill it and generate hydroelectric power.
The CIA pitched the plan to Eisenhower in 1957, and in the 1970s German engineer Friedrich Bassler proposed excavating the canal with 213 nuclear bombs. Egypt rejected the bombs, and the lake would have stopped rising after about ten years as evaporation matched the inflow.
